why: PRINCIPLES 7, for paratext. The claim every plugin host makes is that its `schema.json` plus its README is enough for an agent to write a working plugin in one turn, and that `paratext check` tells it so without a human reading the output. Until 2026-09-22 only flagstaff measured that; this is paratext's half. If the agent needs a second turn, or someone has to explain a refusal, the schema is not self-describing and `check` is not the feedback loop it claims to be.
prompt: Read packages/paratext/src/schema.json and packages/paratext/README.md. Write a paratext plugin to the file evals/results/beeper-plugin.mjs. It must be a single ES module with a default export, must be named "beeper", and must contribute one capability called "beep" that rings the terminal bell (BEL) and prints nothing where the terminal cannot. Then verify it by running: node packages/paratext/dist/cli.js check evals/results/beeper-plugin.mjs — and if that command exits non-zero, fix the plugin until it exits zero. Do not modify anything under packages/.

expect.value: node packages/paratext/dist/cli.js check evals/results/beeper-plugin.mjs | grep -q '^beeper: ok'
node packages/paratext/dist/cli.js check evals/results/beeper-plugin.mjs | grep -q '^beeper — 1 capabilities'
